name: Bandipur Bazaar (Old Town)
tagline: The car-free Newari heart of Bandipur
description: The main pedestrian street lined with restored Newari trading houses, wooden-latticed facades, temples, and the central Tundikhel square. Nearly everything a visitor needs, guesthouses, restaurants, cafes, and shops, sits within a five-minute walk. No vehicles are allowed on the cobbled main street, making it Bandipur's calmest and most photogenic base.
pros: Highest concentration of food and lodging
cons: Can feel touristy midday with day-trippers

name: Tundikhel Viewpoint Area
tagline: The open ridge-top lawn with the mountain panorama
description: A grassy plateau at the edge of the bazaar used historically as a parade ground, now Bandipur's prime spot for unobstructed Annapurna, Manaslu, and Dhaulagiri views at sunrise and sunset. A few guesthouses and viewpoint cafes cluster nearby, and paragliding launches occasionally operate from here. Quieter than the bazaar core but still an easy walk to shops and food.
pros: Best unobstructed Himalayan views in town
cons: Views vanish entirely in cloud or monsoon

name: Ramkot and Siddha Cave Side
tagline: Rural terraced village leading to Nepal's largest cave chamber
description: A cluster of farming hamlets on the slopes below Bandipur bazaar, reached via a scenic downhill trail past terraced fields to Siddha Cave, a vast limestone cavern popular with day hikers. This side of town is rural and undeveloped, with only a few homestays, offering a quieter, more agricultural counterpoint to the bazaar's tourist bustle.
pros: Access to Siddha Cave and forest trails
cons: Very limited lodging and dining options
Trail can be muddy and leech-prone in monsoon

name: Dumre (Gateway Junction Town)
tagline: The highway junction base at the foot of Bandipur's access road
description: A busy roadside town on the Prithvi Highway between Kathmandu and Pokhara, where buses and jeeps transfer passengers for the steep climb up to Bandipur. Dumre has basic hotels, ATMs, and eateries and functions as a practical overnight or transit base for travelers arriving late or catching early onward transport, rather than a scenic destination itself.
bestFor: transit stopovers, early departures, budget transport connections
pros: Reliable ATMs and highway bus connections
Convenient jump-off point for the uphill ride
cons: No hilltop views or historic charm
